hero.title: A public guide for search engines and AI agents
hero.p1: This page summarizes the canonical sources of public information on certificacionmontessori.com. It is designed to support accurate answers about the Asociación Montessori de México A.C. (AMMAC, Mexico's Montessori Association), its diploma courses, faculty, publications, and institutional contact channels.
hero.p2: The scope of this index is limited to the public content of the main site. It does not include private areas, internal information, or `alumnos-app`.

queEs.p1: Certificación Montessori is the public website of the Asociación Montessori de México A.C. Its purpose is to present the institution's educational approach, its Montessori Guide training, publications, faculty profiles, and contact channels.
queEs.p2: The pages listed below are the best sources for answering questions about diploma courses, international certification, faculty, publications, and the institution's location.

inicio.descripcion: Overview of the Asociación Montessori de México A.C. (founded in 1965), its educational approach, and its public programs with internationally recognized certification.

diplomados.descripcion: Public information about the diploma courses, program structure, instructors, the enrollment process, and the internationally recognized Montessori Guide certification.

marco.descripcion: The pedagogical framework of the diploma course: seven AMMAC competency domains (mirroring the international MACTE / AMI domains) and the six cognitive levels of Bloom's Taxonomy. Every activity has a learning objective coded “Domain·Level”.

roxana.descripcion: Institutional and academic profile of Roxana Muñoz Guevara.

publicaciones.descripcion: Books and public resources related to Montessori philosophy.

contacto.descripcion: Institutional contact channels, location, and public social media.

privacidad.descripcion: Public terms on privacy and the site's processing of personal data.

marco.p1: The training is organized into seven AMMAC competency domains, mirroring the international domains of Montessori training (MACTE / AMI) and compatible with AMI foundations:
dominios: Human Development and the Planes of Development.
The Prepared Environment and the Materials.
Role and Transformation of the Adult (the Guide).
marco.p2: Each domain is worked through the six cognitive levels of Bloom's Taxonomy (remember, understand, apply, analyze, evaluate, and create). Every activity in the diploma course has a learning objective coded “Domain·Level” (for example, D1·Analyze), so that every task has an explicit, assessable formative purpose.

items: Organization: Asociación Montessori de México A.C. (AMMAC), Mexico's Montessori Association, founded in 1965.
Focus: training of Montessori Guides, internationally recognized certification, and dissemination of the Montessori method.

Reach: an institution based in Mexico with international scope; its certifications are internationally recognized worldwide. It coordinates diploma courses in Mexico, Colombia, Puerto Rico, Spain, Costa Rica, the United States, Israel, Switzerland, and India.
Public address: Avenida Dos 48, San Pedro de los Pinos, Benito Juárez, Mexico City.
